title: Exposure to natural disasters and vaccination indicators: a systematic review and directions for future research.
authors: Shea B, Shaman J
abstract: Global routine childhood immunization has stagnated for almost two decades, leaving children vulnerable to both immediate and long-term health risks from infectious diseases. Identifying and mitigating impediments to childhood vaccination, such as barriers resulting from exposure to natural disasters, is vital for maintaining population health. While there is general understanding that disasters have the potential to disrupt vaccination services, well designed studies on the degree to which exposure to natural disasters affects vaccination indicators are limited. Understanding the effects of natural disasters on vaccine preventable diseases is an important area for future research as some natural disasters are becoming more frequent and intense due to climate change. To understand the current state of research on exposure to natural disasters and vaccination indicators (i.e., vaccination metrics including administration, coverage, rates), we conducted a systematic literature review of all literature in Embase, Google Scholar, PubMed, and Web of Science up until September 11-12, 2025. We aimed to identify relevant peer reviewed literature focusing on natural disasters and immunization and to assess them for relevance and inclusion. Seventeen studies met the criteria for inclusion. These studies examined the relationship between exposure to cyclones/hurricanes, droughts, earthquakes, flooding, heat waves, and multiple disaster types and changes in vaccination among different age groups. Most (16/17 (94.12%)) papers identified a connection or association between exposure to natural disasters and reduced vaccination indicators. The majority (13/17 (76.47%)) of studies focused on early-childhood vaccinations. Characteristics that affect vulnerability to under-vaccination-exposure level, geographical location, socioeconomic status-were assessed in several papers. Areas for future research include quantifying the degree to which different disaster types affect multiple vaccination indicators within the same individuals and changes in communities over time.

title: Acute multi-organ dysfunction (aMOD): Brighton Collaboration case definition and guidelines for data collection, analysis, and presentation of immunization safety data.
authors: O'Connor C, Jacob ST, Levy JH, Nwagha T, Ramesh D, Munoz FM, Farnon EC, Law B
abstract: This is a new Brighton Collaboration case definition of acute multi-organ dysfunction (aMOD) as an adverse event following immunization (AEFI). It is intended for use in clinical trials and post-licensure pharmacovigilance activities to facilitate safety data comparability across multiple settings. It is not intended to guide clinical management, but it can serve as an outcome measure of disease severity in the context of vaccine efficacy and effectiveness studies. The case definition was developed by a group of subject matter and Brighton Collaboration process experts as part of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI)-funded Safety Platform for Evaluation of vACcines (SPEAC). The Brighton Collaboration case definition includes a scoping review of the literature and expert consensus used to define levels of diagnostic certainty (LOC) for aMOD and provides specific guidelines for related data collection and analysis. The document underwent peer review by a Reference Group of vaccine safety stakeholders and aMOD experts to ensure case definition useability, applicability, and scientific integrity. aMOD is defined as acute dysfunction involving two or more of six organ systems: respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, neurologic, hepatic, and hemostatic. A key feature is the requirement that organ dysfunction occur within the same clinical episode, with onset within 7 days, allowing sequential or simultaneous involvement. Five LOC are included for each of the six organs. The overall aMOD case definition also comprises five LOC categories: Level 1 (Definite), Level 2 (Probable), Level 3 (Possible), Level 4 (Insufficient information), and Level 5 (Not a case). The criteria build on established organ dysfunction frameworks while adapting them for global application. Importantly, AEFI case definitions are separate from causality assessment. This case definition provides a standardized approach to aMOD case ascertainment, bridging concepts of organ dysfunction with Brighton Collaboration requirements for reproducible vaccine safety assessment. It also provides a standard case definition that can be used by stakeholders to harmonize assessment of AEFI to enable rigorous analysis and comparison of AEFI surveillance across settings and studies.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
authors: Athlin Å, Lisspers K, Hasselgren M, Ställberg B, Sandelowsky H, Giezeman M, Janson C, Kisiel MA
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02. CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

title: Differential mortality risks associated with ambient temperature among migrants and non-migrants: a space-time-stratified case-crossover study of the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort (2000-2020).
authors: Firouraghi N, Cortes TR, Jacobson LV, Neves DJD, Silveira IH, Hajat S, Barreto ML, Pescarini JM
abstract: BACKGROUND: Climate change disproportionately affects socially minoritized populations, but migrants' vulnerability to extreme temperatures remains overlooked. We estimated short-term associations between extreme ambient temperatures and mortality among migrants and non-migrants across Brazil. METHODS: We linked the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort to mortality and temperature data (2000-2020) and conducted a space-time-stratified case-crossover study analysing the differential effects of extreme temperature on mortality among internal migrants (i.e., Individuals whose state of birth was different from their residence at registration or death) and non-migrants. We used conditional quasi-Poisson regression with distributed lag non-linear model (DLNM) to estimate relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause non-accidental and cause-specific mortality associated with extreme-cold (1st percentile) and extreme-heat (99th percentile) compared to minimum-mortality-temperature (i.e., the temperature associated with the lowest mortality risk), over 0-20 days in both groups. We further stratified by age, literacy, urbanicity and housing conditions. FINDINGS: We included 1,199,636 deaths among internal-migrants (mean age at death = 62.67 years (standard-deviation (SD) = 18.36), with 673,166 (56%) males) and 3,716,900 deaths among non-migrants (57.18 years (SD = 20.31), with 2,135,293 (57%) males). Over 0-20 days, we observed a consistent pattern of higher risks of all-cause, non-accidental mortality among internal-migrants than non-migrants following both extreme-heat (RRMig(95%CI):1.05(1.01-1.10) vs. RRNon-mig:1.01(0.99-1.04)) and extreme-cold (RRMig:1.27(1.22-1.32) vs. RRNon-mig:1.24(1.20-1.28)). Extreme cold-related circulatory mortality (mortality due to diseases of the circulatory system, based on the relevant International Classification of Diseases codes) (I00-I99) was higher among non-migrants (RRMig:1.32(1.20-1.45) vs. RRNon-mig:1.41(1.31-1.51)) while heat-related respiratory mortality (J00-J99) was higher among internal-migrants (RRMig:1.32(1.10-1.58) vs. RRNon-mig:1.06(1.00-1.17)), particularly those illiterate (RRMig:1.84(1.25-2.71) vs. RRNon-mig:1.10(0.89-1.36)). Other subcategories showed greater 95%CI overlap. INTERPRETATION: We found internal migrants are likely to experience higher heat-related respiratory mortality than non-migrants particularly low-educated migrants. Our results highlight the need to further consider migrants for targeted climate adaptation policies, with a focus on reducing social inequalities in the place of arrival. FUNDING: The Wellcome Trust.

title: Liver fibrosis risk, missed follow-up, and inequitable specialist referral in the All of Us Research Program: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sellers K, White TM, Manolas MI, Hagström H, Brennan PN, Diaz LA, Bansal MB, Danpanichkul P
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently undiagnosed, despite liver fibrosis being the strongest predictor of liver-related morbidity and mortality. We aimed to quantify Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index-based fibrosis risk and to evaluate guideline-recommended follow-up-FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialist referral-in a large US cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of electronic health record data from the US All of Us Research Program. Among adults aged 35 years or older with sufficient laboratory data, FIB-4 scores were calculated from routinely captured biomarkers, classified as low (<1.3), indeterminate (1.3-2.67; 2.0-2.67 if aged ≥65 years), or high risk (>2.67), and described across sociodemographic and metabolic subgroups; associations with incident major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) were assessed with Cox proportional-hazards regression. We examined FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialty referrals within 365 days of the index FIB-4 date. FINDINGS: Among 136,004 participants (mean age 60.8 years [SD 13.5]; 79,365 [58.4%] female; 81,420 [59.9%] White, 21,779 [16.0%] Hispanic or Latino, 20,076 [14.8%] Black), 26,971 (19.8%, 95% CI 19.6-20.0) had indeterminate and 11,217 (8.2%, 8.1-8.4) high FIB-4-based fibrosis risk. Elevated risk was more frequent with cardiovascular disease (41.7% vs 25.6%), hypertension (30.7% vs 23.4%), and type 2 diabetes (29.7% vs 27.4%), rising from 25.6% with no metabolic comorbidities to 36.6% with four. FIB-4 documentation was rare, and fewer than 1% of high-risk participants underwent confirmatory testing or referral; referral was low across risk categories (0.19% high, 0.19% indeterminate, 0.25% low risk). MALO occurred in 1308 (11.7%) high-risk vs 830 (0.8%) low-risk participants (adjusted hazard ratio 19.68, 95% CI 17.88-21.67). INTERPRETATION: Routinely collected laboratory data identify substantial liver fibrosis risk in this volunteer US cohort, yet guideline-recommended follow-up is uncommon. Implementation strategies such as automated risk calculation and reflex-based testing pathways could reduce missed opportunities for earlier diagnosis and intervention. FUNDING: No specific funding was received for this study.

title: Polymeric and metallic occluders for interventional therapy of cardiovascular diseases.
authors: Liu R, Wang Q, Ding J
abstract: Interventional therapy has, as a minimally invasive approach, been widely adopted for treating cardiovascular diseases, particularly structural heart disease, where occluders play a pivotal role in transcatheter closure. This paper comprehensively reviews the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of cardiovascular occluders, beginning with their interventional applications in congenital heart defects (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent foramen ovale, and patent ductus arteriosus) and left atrial appendage closure. The focus then shifts to occluder materials and design principles, tracing the progression from early non-degradable metals like stainless steel to the current gold standard, nitinol, whose hyperelasticity enables self-expanding devices. To promote rapid endothelialization on nitinol implants, surface nanocoatings of bioceramics such as titanium nitride have been developed to modulate cell-material interactions. To eliminate risks from permanent metallic implants, biodegradable occluders have emerged as an alternative. The design of biodegradable occluders utilizing medical polymers such as polylactic acid and polydioxanone is illustrated, highlighting structural innovations such as locking strategies to overcome the lack of hyperelasticity. Key considerations including matching degradation rate with tissue regeneration and achieving X-ray visibility are also described. Finally, future perspectives are presented: expanding applications to infants and the elderly, incorporating tissue engineering for in situ regeneration, and leveraging nanotechnology and artificial intelligence to optimize device performance. The ongoing advancement of occluder technologies will propel interventional therapy for structural heart disease toward a safer and more effective treatment.

title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
authors: Yu Z, Dong X, Li F, Zhang Y, Dai S, Cao N, Jia X, Zhao J
abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

title: Transposable elements as dual agents in livestock-parasite interactions: From parasite adaptation to host genetic innovation.
authors: Omara A, Moawad AS, Ge J, Geng T
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs), which were previously seen as genomic parasites, are currently viewed as major contributors to evolutionary innovation in host-parasite interactions. This review provides an overview of the current knowledge of TEs in veterinary parasitology, divided into three interlinked levels. Firstly, in terms of parasite genome biology, TEs are highly diverse and actively transposing, from the extremely active mobilomes of strongylid nematodes and liver flukes to the TE-rich but genomically reduced microsporidian parasites. Secondly, at the host-parasite interface, direct physical contacts help in the horizontal exchange of TEs between the parasites and their hosts. Thirdly, TE activity leads to important functional innovations, including expansions of virulence-related gene families in schistosomes, formation of species-specific stage-regulated non-coding RNAs in liver flukes, and even TE-derived small interfering RNAs secreted by parasitic nematodes as cross-species immune modulators. On the host side, polymorphic TEs, especially SINEs and endogenous retroviruses, provide abundant opportunities to generate phenotypic diversity in livestock by affecting features such as muscle formation, fat accumulation, fur coloration, and immune response. Throughout this review, we clearly separate the established facts from the associations and hypotheses, and highlight the areas of knowledge deficit. In conclusion, we will outline the model of utilizing TE biomarkers in selective breeding, and note that the association between particular polymorphisms of TEs and resistance to parasites is mostly hypothetical and needs further verification.

title: When the earth shakes on fragile foundations: the Venezuelan earthquakes and two decades of public health system erosion.
authors: Paníz-Mondolfi AE, Chaccour C, Carrión-Nessi FS, Acosta-Serrano Á, Zambrano O, Gabaldón-Figueira JC, Grillet ME
abstract: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

title: Microbiome changes following immigration: Rethinking "Westernization" as an explanatory concept.
authors: Sharma R, Holcomb LE, Ishaq SL, O'Doherty KC
abstract: An emerging focus in microbiome science is on changes to people's microbiomes following immigration, particularly to so-called Western countries, such as the USA, Canada, and Australia. Moving to these regions has been linked to microbiome changes that may increase immigrants' susceptibility to health problems, including obesity and Inflammatory Bowel Disease. The term "Westernization" (and adjacent terminology) is frequently used to describe changes in diet, lifestyle, and built environment - and the consequent microbiome shifts - associated with immigration. However, what Westernization means in this context, and whether it is an appropriate descriptor, is often unclear. The purpose of this article is to provide a review of the diverse meanings associated with the terms "West", "Western", "Westernization" (and similar) across microbiome-related research and broader uses. We argue that these terms can obscure the specific structural, environmental, and cultural factors shaping microbiome changes. We discuss the consequences of this imprecision and provide recommendations for future research. Avoiding oversimplified conclusions about what impacts immigrants' microbiome and health can contribute to more accurate targets for public health interventions for these groups in the long term.

title: Unsolved problems with ENaC: From molecules to mammals.
authors: Palmer LG
abstract: The epithelial Na channel (ENaC) mediates transport of Na+ in the kidney, the colon, the lung, and the sweat and salivary ducts. The activity of these channels is highly regulated and contributes to the maintenance of total body Na+, extracellular fluid volume, and plasma K+. Defects in the channel itself or in its regulation are implicated in hypertension and in other diseases. Despite progress in revealing many aspects of ENaC biology, many important questions remain unanswered. These include the following: What determines the remarkable ion selectivity of the channel? How is the channel directed to the apical plasma membrane? How does aldosterone regulate the channel? What is its role in producing urine with minimal Na+? And to what extent does the channel contribute to essential hypertension, cystic fibrosis, nephrotic syndrome, and liver failure? Here, I will discuss these questions and how they relate to our current understanding of the roles of ENaC in health and disease.

title: Genomic and biological characterization of ΦAB114, a temperate siphovirus infecting colistin- and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
authors: Uluçam Atay G, Alpay Karaoğlu Ş, Bozdeveci A, Suyabatmaz Ş, Bayramoğlu G
abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is a prominent opportunistic pathogen responsible for healthcare-associated infections. Its increasing association with multidrug resistance (MDR) severely constrains current therapeutic options, underlining the urgent need for alternative antimicrobial strategies. In this study, we aimed to isolate and comprehensively characterize a novel bacteriophage, ΦAB114, targeting MDR A. baumannii through morphological, biological, and genomic analyses. ΦAB114 was characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), host range analysis, and Illumina-based whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Functional genome annotation, comparative genomics, and phylogenetic analyses were performed to determine its genetic features, evolutionary relationships, and the presence of antibiotic resistance or virulence-associated genes. TEM analysis revealed that ΦAB114 exhibits a siphovirus-like morphology and belongs to the class Caudoviricetes. ΦAB114 was able to infect 20 of 72 clinical A. baumannii isolates, including carbapenem- and colistin-resistant strains WGS identified a putatively linear double-stranded DNA genome of 37,423 bp with a GC content of 39.76%, encoding 55 putative ORFs. Functional annotation revealed genes involved in structural assembly, DNA packaging, replication, and regulation, while an integrase gene suggested a temperate lifestyle. Comparative genomic and phylogenetic analyses showed high sequence similarity to Acinetobacter phages Ab105-1phi and AbTJ. No antibiotic resistance or virulence-associated genes were detected. The genomic characteristics of ΦAB114, the absence of detectable antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes, and its observed activity against MDR A. baumannii clinical isolates contribute to the genomic and biological characterization of this temperate phage, underscoring the need for further experimental studies to fully evaluate its biological behavior and potential applications.

title: Rare-earth-free magnesium-zinc alloy with controlled biodegradation and biocompatibility for novel biodegradable metallic stent.
authors: Park Y, Ha Y, Roh HJ, Lee H, Eo SJ, Kang DY, Lee N, Jung HD
abstract: Biodegradable magnesium (Mg) alloy stents offer a transient alternative to permanent metallic implants; however, clinically used WE43 contains rare-earth (RE) elements, raising concerns regarding the long-term biosafety of RE-containing degradation products and their potential tissue accumulation. Here, we investigated two RE-free Mg-Zinc (Zn)-based alloys, MZ01 (Mg-1Zn-0.1Ca) and ZM115 (Mg-1Zn-1.5Mn-0.5Sr), and established a mechanistic cascade linking alloy composition and microstructure to electrochemical analyses revealed alloy-dependent differences in grain structure and interfacial corrosion resistance, with MZ01 exhibiting the highest charge-transfer resistance. In a mouse subcutaneous model, MZ01 showed more uniform degradation, smaller and more rapidly resolving hydrogen gas cavities, and a significantly lower microcrack area fraction at Day 56 than WE43 and ZM115, accompanied by attenuated inflammatory and fibrotic responses. In the rabbit iliac arteries, all stents maintained luminal patency without thrombosis through 56 days, while MZ01 exhibited lower neointimal thickness, lower perivascular apoptosis and late inflammation, and enhanced early endothelialization compared with WE43. Preliminary descriptive porcine coronary implantation further demonstrated the technical feasibility and sustained patency of MZ01 over 56 days. Collectively, these findings define a composition-microstructure-corrosion-cellular response-vascular healing axis and identify MZ01 as a RE-free Mg-Zn alloy with controlled biodegradation and favorable biocompatibility, supporting its further development as a biodegradable cardiovascular scaffold.

title: Microfluidic integrated nucleic acid test (MINT) enabled by coupling FEN1-aided RPA with wax-purification and bead-carrier.
authors: Xu Z, Gao X, Huang J, Pang S, Wang S, Wang Y, Feng L, Ma Y
abstract: To guide timely antibiotic treatment, a tool for quick antimicrobial resistance gene detection is required. Here a Microfluidic Integrated Nucleic Acid Test platform (namely, MINT) was proposed for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. The platform integrates fast nucleic acid extraction based on hybrid wax-phase purification, and DNA amplification based on our newly developed FEN1-aided RPA (FARPA) into a microfluidic chip. The wax-phase stays solid at room temperature, while becomes liquid at >50 °C to allow the wash of inhibitors carried from extraction buffer, thus the chip keeps stable during storage and transportation. The movement of extracted DNA bound with magnetic beads were controlled by a magnet. The beaded DNA was quickly purified during the flow through the wax phase, and the amplification started once the beaded DNA reached to the well for FARPA. The signal from target-positive sample could be readily sensed by a conventional smartphone. The turnaround time is about 40 min from the sample to the result. The platform was validated by detecting the blaKPC-2 resistance gene of Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) from urine samples with the reliable detection concentration of 500 CFU/mL, achieving 100% agreement for the 29 clinical urine samples (19 positive, 10 negative) with conventional qPCR. It is easy to adapt the MINT to any other pathogen only by designing the corresponding primers and probes for FARPA. It is promising to apply MINT for bed-site antimicrobial resistance screening just after operation.

title: Integrated profiling of β-lactam susceptibility and spoilage-associated enzyme activities in psychrotrophic bacteria from the raw milk production chain.
authors: Hu X, Lei Y, Kong Z, Pang X, Shen J, Wang S
abstract: Psychrotrophic bacteria are important targets for microbiological control of cold-chain raw milk because of their ability to produce spoilage-associated enzymes and harbor antimicrobial resistance determinants. However, these two functional characteristics are often investigated separately, leaving their co-occurrence within the same isolate collection insufficiently characterized. To address this gap, 543 dominant culturable bacterial isolates were recovered from raw milk and dairy-farm-associated samples collected from six regions of China. Pseudomonas was the most prevalent genus, followed by Acinetobacter, Chryseobacterium, Serratia, and Psychrobacter. β-Lactam minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) distributions varied substantially among genera, with Chryseobacterium exhibiting the highest proportion of β-lactamase-associated phenotype-positive isolates. Among 226 raw-milk isolates screened using ceftazidime, all 44 isolates showing inhibitor-responsive or carbapenemase-associated phenotypes were subjected to whole-genome sequencing. Genome-wide resistance-gene screening identified annotated β-lactamase genes predominantly in Chryseobacterium and Acinetobacter. In contrast, the resistance-related annotations retained in phenotype-positive Pseudomonas isolates were mainly associated with efflux systems and adaptive response mechanisms. In the integrated analysis, a relative MIC-enzyme risk-prioritization score ranked Serratia (0.88), Chryseobacterium (0.71), and Pseudomonas (0.67) as the three highest-ranking genera. The β-lactam MIC score showed weak positive correlations with the protease-associated score (Spearman's ρ = 0.297, P < 0.001) and with the lipase-associated score (ρ = 0.194, P < 0.001). These findings indicate that genus abundance alone is insufficient to characterize the functional heterogeneity of psychrotrophic bacteria in raw milk. Integrating β-lactam MIC patterns with spoilage-enzyme activity provides complementary information for genus-level prioritization within this isolate collection.

title: Proceedings of the 3rd edition of the International e-Health Forum 2024.
Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authors: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
authors: Wang J, Wang X, Liu S, Zheng Y, Wang C, Cheng J, Wang X
abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

title: Long-term trajectories of invasive hemodynamic parameters and clinical outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation.
authors: Legtenberg S, Ter Maaten JM, Erasmus ME, Kuijpers M, Douglas YL, Droogh JM, de Felice E, van den Broek SAJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term hemodynamic changes after durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation are not well characterized. Characterizing these trajectories is clinically relevant, as persistent or evolving abnormalities in filling pressures and pulmonary circulation may identify patients at risk for adverse outcomes. METHOD: We conducted a retrospective single-center study including all patients who underwent durable LVAD implantation at the University Medical Center Groningen (2012 to 2025). We evaluated serial right heart catheterization (RHC) measurements to describe hemodynamic trajectories. Repeated measures, mixed-effect models were used to analyze hemodynamic trajectories up to 60 months of follow-up, including mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), right atrial pressure (RAP), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). Trajectories were compared according to survivor status, baseline LVAD strategy, development of late right ventricular failure (RVF), presence of aortic regurgitation (AR), and worsening renal function (WRF). RESULTS: Among 199 patients (176 HeartMate 3; 23 HeartMate II), mean PAP (-10.1 mmHg, 95% CI -13.1 to -7.1) and PCWP (-9.9 mmHg, 95% CI -12.5 to -7.2) decreased significantly within the first 6 months after LVAD implantation, while RAP (0.0 mmHg, 95% CI -0.8 to 0.8) remained unchanged. Cardiac index (+0.6 L/min/m², 95% CI 0.4-0.8) and cardiac output (+1.3 L/min, 95% CI 0.9-1.7) increased significantly over the same interval. Beyond 6 months, trajectories for most hemodynamic parameters remained generally stable. Non-survivors and patients developing late RVF showed consistently higher filling pressures with trajectories largely parallel to those of survivors or those without RVF. Hemodynamic trajectories did not differ by initial LVAD strategy. In contrast, clinically significant aortic regurgitation and WRF were associated with distinct hemodynamic trajectories. CONCLUSION: Hemodynamic parameters after durable LVAD implantation improved early and remained largely stable thereafter. Patients with adverse clinical outcomes showed persistently higher and/or altered hemodynamic profiles. These findings suggest that longitudinal hemodynamic assessment may enable early identification of patients at risk for adverse outcomes.

title: Preliminary experience with controlled hypothermic storage of donor heart in combined heart transplantation.
authors: Argaw ST, Lora Ronco L, Frering A, Kloeckner M, Coutance G, Coilly A, Vibert E, Snanoudj R
abstract: While studies have demonstrated improved clinical outcomes with the use of controlled hypothermic storage (CHS) devices in isolated heart transplantation, it has not been evaluated in combined heart transplantation. In this small retrospective study (n=17), we evaluate clinical outcomes after combined heart-liver and heart-kidney transplantation in recipients of donor hearts preserved with conventional ice cold storage (ICS, n=10) versus CHS (n=7). The study found severe early graft dysfunction (EGD) occurred more frequently in the ICS cohort when compared to the CHS cohort (70% vs 0%, respectively). In addition, the CHS cohort had shorter median intensive care unit length of stay (7 days compared to 15.5 days, respectively) as well as fewer post-transplant complications, including sepsis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS), pneumonia (40% in ICS and 14.3% in CHS), stroke (30% in ICS and 0% in CHS), and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS). These preliminary findings suggest CHS may improve outcomes in combined heart transplantation.

title: From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
authors: Peng S, Liu Q, Duan C, Liu J, Wang R, Huang Y, Long A, Deng Q
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

title: Population attributable mortality associated with respiratory viruses in Ontario, Canada: a population-based ecological analysis.
authors: Fisman DN, Grima AA, Wilson NJ, Mann S, Tuite AR, Lee CE
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this. We estimated the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada, over 1993-2025, across the pandemic transition. METHODS: We analysed monthly all-cause mortality with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, influenza B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fitted for pre-pandemic (1993-2020) and combined pandemic (2020-2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions. Further analyses examined temporal stratification, exclusion of the early pandemic period, and models without Fourier adjustment. FINDINGS: Pre-pandemic, influenza A was associated with 1.8% (95% CI 1.4-2.3) of mortality; influenza B showed no association; RSV showed positive associations (1.9%, 1.3-2.4) only without seasonal adjustment. Amid elevated pandemic mortality (IRR 1.052, p < 0.0001), SARS-CoV-2 was associated with 6.48% (4.5-8.4) of deaths, 3-4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden. Attributable deaths (18,052) fell within 3% of 18,594 independently adjudicated Ontario COVID-19 deaths. Post-Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) SARS-CoV-2 mortality (9.8%, 1.1-17.7) did not differ from PHEIC estimates; post-PHEIC influenza did not differ from pre-pandemic baselines. INTERPRETATION: SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3-4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures, and continued to contribute beyond the formal emergency period, underscoring the importance of sustained respiratory virus prevention. FUNDING: Canadian Institutes of Health Research.

title: 45th International Symposium on Intensive Care & Emergency Medicine.
Bioactive shape-memory biodegradable biliary stent functionalized with dHAM-Curcumin for improved biliary repair and microenvironment modulation.
authors: Dai C, Zhang H, Bai Y, Guan X, Li R, Quan D, Ding Y, Rao Z
abstract: Anastomotic stricture after biliodigestive reconstruction remains a clinical challenge leading to recurrent cholangitis, jaundice, and secondary biliary cirrhosis. Conventional plastic stents provide temporary support but are prone to biofilm formation and biliary sludge accumulation and require secondary removal procedures. There is a need for biodegradable biliary stents that provide sufficient mechanical support while actively modulating the local microenvironment. A biodegradable shape-memory biliary stent composed of a poly(CL-co-TOSUO)/BaSO4 (PCT/BaSO4) composite core coated with a decellularized human amniotic membrane-curcumin (dHAM-Cur) hydrogel was developed. In vivo performance was assessed in rat subcutaneous and duodenal implantation models and in a rabbit orthotopic common bile duct stenting model. Gut microbiota and bile metabolomic changes were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS). The PCT/BaSO4 stent exhibited suitable mechanical properties, radiopacity, and shape memory functionality, with a degradation profile that matched the expected biliary healing period. The dHAM-Cur coating increased surface hydrophilicity and supported sustained curcumin release. The functionalized stent reduced inflammatory cell infiltration, fibrous capsule formation, and bile duct fibrosis, and preserved biliary patency compared with plastic and PCL/BaSO4 controls in vivo. Multi-omics analyses suggested that the stent subtly reshaped gut microbial composition and modulated bile acid-related metabolic pathways. The PCT/BaSO4@dHAM-Cur composite demonstrated local anti-inflammatory and anti-adhesion effects in preclinical models, along with favorable biocompatibility and anti-restenotic potential. This system holds promise as a therapeutic platform for the clinical management of biliodigestive anastomoses.

title: Hematopoietic cell transplantation using treosulfan-based conditioning for IL-10 receptor deficiency.
authors: Lakkaraja M, Schmitt EG, Sood AK, Chen K, Modi AJ, Verbsky JW, Torgerson T, Wahbeh G
abstract: IL-10 receptor deficiency is a life-threatening inborn error of immunity associated with early-onset inflammatory bowel disease. Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using treosulfan-based conditioning resulted in excellent survival with full donor engraftment. Importantly, anakinra effectively served as a bridge to HCT.

title: DUF6383-domain containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis predicts survival in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
authors: Kreimeyer H, Gonzalez C, Fondevila MF, AlcHepNet Investigators, Canbay A, Stärkel P, Gonzalez DJ, Schnabl B
abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis is a hallmark of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) characterized by a higher abundance of unfavorable species and a reduction of beneficial species. In this study, we aimed to analyze the bacterial proteome of stool samples from patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) (n = 80), alcohol use disorder (AUD; n = 20), and controls (n = 19) from an international multicenter cohort using quantitative tandem mass tag (TMT)-based metaproteomic profiling. We validated our results in an independent multicenter cohort of 72 patients with AH at the genomic level using qPCR. We detected 2,364 bacterial proteins and identified distinct metaproteomic signatures separating controls, patients with AUD, and AH. Patients with AUD and AH were characterized by depletion of Firmicutes-derived proteins and enrichment of proteins from Bacteroidetes, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria. Eighteen bacterial proteins increased with disease severity, many with multifunctional "moonlighting" roles, including enolase and hexokinase. DUF6383 domain-containing protein from Parabacteroides distasonis is correlated with histological injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, and is linked to neutrophil degranulation in the host. Patients with a high abundance of DUF6383 domain-containing protein had significantly lower 90-day survival, and this association was validated by qPCR at the genomic level in a second cohort. Our findings show that microbial proteins are associated with disease severity and progression, and that DUF6383 domain-containing protein from P. distasonis is a potential prognostic biomarker for AH.

title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.
authors: Okuma H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions. RESULTS: After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables. CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00941-2.

ALMS1 stabilizes the proximal centriole to drive transition zone assembly and ciliogenesis.
authors: Phan TP, Derderian C, Herranz-Pérez V, Li KH, Burlingame AL, Reiter JF
abstract: The human ciliopathy Alström syndrome is caused by mutations in ALMS1. How ALMS1 contributes to cilia function has been unclear. Unlike other ciliopathy-associated proteins, ALMS1 localizes to the proximal end of centrioles, raising the possibility that it contributes to cilia function via a distinct mechanism. We found that, without ALMS1, centrioles are short and frequently break at their proximal ends. Truncated, broken ALMS1 mutant centrioles display reduced microtubule-organizing activity and disrupted centriole linkers. Without ALMS1, Golgi-derived cargos, including transmembrane components of the transition zone, are impaired in their trafficking to the centrosome. Consequently, ALMS1 is important for transition zone assembly, ciliogenesis, and the control of ciliary membrane composition. In mice, disruption of ALMS1 causes progressive, age-dependent loss of cilia in tissues affected in Alström syndrome, including retina, kidney, and brain. We conclude that Alström syndrome is caused by disruption of proximal centriole integrity and centrosome-directed protein trafficking, compromising ciliary assembly and maintenance.
